take: Buying has shifted from consumers to central banks: jewellery tonnes -17% while central banks +62%, each vs Q2 2025.
Central banks: Q2 was a record second quarter, but the first half (345 t) was the lowest since 2022, after WGC cut Q1 to 57 t (from 244 t).
Jewellery spending in dollars still rose (first half +22% vs a year earlier, $86bn, WGC press release): fewer tonnes at a much higher price.
Gold ETFs worldwide saw a 44.8 t outflow in Q2 (first half +18 t).

lead: SPDR Gold Shares is Hold, at −26 on a −100 to +100 scale, unchanged from −26 on 28 Oct (scores run as of the 29 Oct close); the call is Hold on 7 of the last 10 trading days, and the price trend improved to −72 from −100 while Demand fell to −7 from +14.
bullets: The price trend is still down, but less so. Price trend scores −72, up from −100 on 28 Oct: GLD is 10.8% below its 200-day average (bearish; it was 9.7% below), its 50-day average is 5.2% below the 200-day (bearish), and gold trails the S&P 500 (SPY) by 4.0 points over 3 months (it trailed by 5.4 points).

The money backdrop is weak. Liquidity scores −40, unchanged from −40: buying vs selling volume is 0.62x (bearish; it was 0.75x), GLD's gold holdings are down 1.2% over 20 trading days against tonnes 20 trading days earlier (neutral, close to the −1.5% bearish line), hedge-fund net long is at the 32nd percentile of its last 3 years (neutral), the dollar backdrop is +0.74 points over 20 days (neutral) and Fed rate expectations are −8.9 points, towards rises (neutral).

Demand weakened to −7 from +14. The 10-year real interest rate is down 0.24 points over 20 trading days (bullish for gold), inflation expectations are down 0.01 points (neutral), and GLD tonnes are up 3.4% over 60 trading days (neutral; it was +3.6%, bullish, and the bullish line is +3.5%). Central bank buying is down 20.5% (780 t vs 981 t for the 4 quarters to Jun 2026) and consumer jewellery plus bars and coins demand is down 10.1% (585 t vs 651 t in Q2 2026); both are bearish and unchanged.

Gold is stretched against its own history but not against stocks. Valuation scores 0, unchanged: GLD is 32.3% above its 200-week average (down from 34.1%, neutral; bearish starts at +60%) and the gold-to-S&P 500 ratio is 9.9% above its 10-year median (down from 10.9%, neutral; bearish starts at +25%).

The call is Hold, and it is now a plain Hold. It was shown as 'price-led weakness' yesterday; today the composite is −26, 7 of the last 10 trading days sit in this zone. GLD closed at $368.57, −1.3% on the day vs −0.3% for the S&P 500; −0.1% over 5 trading days (S&P 500 +0.7%) and −0.8% over 3 months. Closest to flipping: GLD tonnes held, 20-day change (−1.2%, turns bearish at −1.5%) and the dollar backdrop (+0.74 points, turns bearish at +1.00).
defects: The call needs 7 of the last 10 trading days in one zone before it is confirmed; 14 trading days of scores are recorded so far.
The day's move breakdown keeps the stock wording: 'Sector' = SPY's move beyond the S&P 500 (near zero), 'Company-specific' = gold's own move.

Today's zone does not turn on one figure alone, but central bank buying (DM4) reads -20.5% mostly because WGC moved 187 t of Q1 2026 into another category. It counts at half weight (6 of 12 points, Kenneth 1 Oct) until WGC's Q3 2026 report (~29 Oct). On WGC's first Q1 figure DM4 is neutral and the composite about -25 (above the -30 Sell line, so the zone would read Hold).
10-year real rate (G-DM1) is published by FRED a day late: latest value 22 Oct.

Stretch (G-VL1): the 200-week average counts the current week twice (Yahoo repeats it), so today's +36.4% (vs a 200-week average of $275.53) is slightly off; the corrected figure is not computed here. The score is unaffected (bearish only at 60%+); engine fix pending.
Fed odds (LQ6) use the shared engine's 28-day window and are jumpy: rise odds were 48% on 29 Sep and 34% on 30 Sep; on 29 Sep LQ6 would have read bearish (composite about -36).
GLD flows (G-LQ2, G-DM3) cover GLD only, not all gold funds worldwide.
Hedge-fund positioning (G-LQ3) is weekly: latest report as of Tue 6 Oct (the one before was 29 Sep).
Sensitivity to the S&P 500 (0.79x, last 252 trading days) is computed from daily GLD and index moves; gold has been unusually correlated with stocks in 2026.

5-year weekly replay (research/sanity_check.md): Sell readings in 2021-26 were followed by GLD +12.9% over 6 months on average vs +10.8% for all weeks; stretch at extremes was the best input, real rates the weakest.
